walkthroughs.body_html:
Measurements & Errors — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Measurements & Errors brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Measurements & Errors.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A car travels 4 km north then 3 km east. What is its displacement magnitude?
options: 7 km
5 km
1 km
25 km

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
options: Acceleration
Momentum
Kinetic energy
Weight

mcqs.q: Is the cosmological redshift of distant galaxies a true Doppler shift?
options: No — it arises from the expansion of space stretching photon wavelengths during transit, not from the galaxy's motion through space.
No — it is caused by dust in space absorbing blue light.
Yes — it is the same Doppler shift as a moving siren on Earth.
Intensity has no effect on anything in the photoelectric effect.

mcqs.q: How does the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depend on light intensity?
options: Higher intensity gives photoelectrons more kinetic energy.
It does not — max KE depends only on the frequency of the light; intensity affects the rate (number) of electrons emitted.
No — it is caused by dust in space absorbing blue light.
Intensity has no effect on anything in the photoelectric effect.

mcqs.q: What does gravitational field strength at a point represent?
options: The force per unit mass that would act on a test mass placed at that point.
Intensity has no effect on anything in the photoelectric effect.
The mass of the object creating the field.
The total gravitational force at that point regardless of mass.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Acceleration”?
options: Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.
Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Vector”?
options: Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.
A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Velocity”?
options: Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.
Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Resolving vectors”?
options: Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.
Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.
The vector from an initial to a final position; the straight-line change in position.
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Scalar”?
options: Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.
The vector from an initial to a final position; the straight-line change in position.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Displacement”?
options: A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
The vector from an initial to a final position; the straight-line change in position.
A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.
Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.

free_texts.hint: It's one of the six key terms above.
